definition: Germany's standard temporary residence permit — time-limited and tied to a specific purpose, such as work, study or family reunion, unlike the indefinite Niederlassungserlaubnis it can eventually lead to.
longform: Most foreign nationals living in Germany hold an Aufenthaltserlaubnis at some stage, since it is the entry point for nearly every route on this site's Germany coverage. The permit's conditions — what work it allows, whether it can be extended, how it counts toward settlement — depend on which purpose it was granted for, so two Aufenthaltserlaubnis holders can have meaningfully different rights depending on their underlying route.
